title: Rabbi Chiyya the Tall
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Ketubot 104b relates that his mother-in-law was his brother’s wife; his brother died childless, and she summoned him to judgment before Rabbah bar Shila … he wrote her an authorization over his property. He came before Rava; Rabbi Chiyya the Tall said to him, “Let the Master see how they have judged me.” He said to him, “They judged you well.” The reading of the Rif and the Rosh is Rabbi Chiyya the Tall of Difti. In Nedarim 8b: “Rabbi Shimon bar Zevid said that Rabbi Yitzchak bar Tavla said that Rabbi Chiyya the Tall said.” Hyman endorses Seder HaDorot’s question, since Rabbi Yitzchak bar Tavla was much earlier; he supports this by noting that Rabbi Shimon bar Zevid too lived in the days of Rabbi Zeira. Hyman considers the names there undoubtedly corrupted and suggests that the reference is to the Rabbi Chiyya who was tall in his generation.

notes.text: The unusual mother-in-law/brother’s-widow relationship is preserved as supplied and not repaired into a different family. Hyman’s undoubtedly-corrupted judgment and tall-in-his-generation suggestion retain their force and attribution.

The consulted Ketubot 104b connected narrative preserves the mother-in-law/brother’s-wife wording, twenty-five years of support, the suit before Rabbah bar Shila and Chiyya’s appeal to Rava. Rava first says he was judged correctly, then separately finds the written authorization defective. Hyman’s compressed quotation and unusual family wording remain intact. Exact Rif/Rosh Difti readings, the Nedarim-chain dating and undoubtedly-corrupted judgment remain Hyman-attributed.
